speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: So to set a little just foundation for the conversation we're going to have, what are you seeing on the ground within companies trying to build AI products?

speaker: Unknown
en: What's going well?
zh: 哪些方面进展顺利？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's not going well?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think 2025 has been significantly different than 2024.
zh: 我认为 2025 年与 2024 年有着显著不同。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of the use cases that I saw last year were more of slap chat on your data.

en: And this year, a ton of companies are really rethinking their user experiences and their workflows and all of that and really understanding that you need to deconstruct and reconstruct your processes in order to build successful AI products.

en: And that's the good stuff.

speaker: Unknown
en: The bad stuff is the execution is still all over the place.

speaker: Unknown
en: Because previously, I feel like PMs and engineers and all of these folks had their own feedback loops to optimize.
zh: 因为以前，我觉得 PM 和工程师以及所有这些人都拥有自己的反馈循环来优化。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 而现在你们可能需要坐在同一个房间里。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 你们可能正在一起查看智能体轨迹 并决定你的产品应该如何表现。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a tighter form of collaboration.
zh: 所以这是一种更紧密的协作形式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let me follow that thread.

speaker: Unknown
en: We worked on a guest post together that came out a few months ago.

speaker: Unknown
en: And the thing that stood out to me most that stuck with me most after working on that post is this really key insight that building AI products is very different from building non-AI products.
zh: 最让我印象深刻、在撰写那篇文章后一直留在我脑海里的，是这一非常关键的洞察：构建 AI 产品与构建非 AI 产品非常不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the thing that you're big on getting across is there's two very big differences.
zh: 而你们要传达的一个重要观点是，有两个非常大的差异。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about those two differences.
zh: 谈谈这两个差异。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, I want to make sure that we drive home the right point.
zh: 同样，我想确保我们把这一点讲透彻。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are tons of similarities of building AI systems and software systems as well, but then there are some things that kind of fundamentally change the way you build software systems versus AI systems.
zh: 构建 AI 系统和软件系统也有很多相似之处，但有些事情从根本上改变了构建软件系统与 AI 系统的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of them that most people tend to ignore is the non-determinism.
zh: 其中一个大多数人倾向于忽略的是非确定性。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're pretty much working with a non-deterministic API as compared to traditional software.
zh: 与传统软件相比，你几乎是在与非确定性 API 打交道。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does that mean and why does that have to affect us is in traditional software, you pretty much have a very well-mapped decision engine or workflow.
zh: 这意味着什么以及为什么它会影响我们，在于在传统软件中，你有一个非常清晰的决策引擎或工作流。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think of something like Booking.com.
zh: 想想像 Booking.com 这样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have an intention that you want to make a booking in San Francisco for two nights, et cetera.
zh: 你有一个意图，你想在旧金山预订两晚的住宿，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: The product has kind of been built so that your intention can be converted into a particular action and you kind of are clicking through a bunch of buttons, options, forms, and all of that, and you finally achieve your intention.
zh: 产品的构建方式使得你的意图可以转化为特定的行动，你基本上是一路点击一堆按钮、选项、表单等等，最终实现了你的意图。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now that layer in AI products has completely been replaced by a very fluid interface, which is mostly natural language, which means the user can literally come up with a ton of ways of saying or communicating their intentions.
zh: 但现在在 AI 产品中，那一层已经被一个非常流畅的界面完全取代了，主要是自然语言，这意味着用户实际上可以用大量方式来表达或传达他们的意图。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that kind of changes a lot of things because now you don't know how your user's going to be here.
zh: 这改变了很多事情，因为现在你不知道你的用户将如何在这里出现。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's on the input side.
zh: 这是在输入端。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the output is also that you're working with a non-deterministic probabilistic API, which is your LLM.
zh: 输出也是你在使用一个非确定性的概率性 API，也就是你的 LLM。

speaker: Unknown
en: And LLMs are pretty sensitive to prompt phrasings and they're pretty much black boxes.
zh: 并且 LLM 对提示词措辞非常敏感，而且它们基本上是黑盒。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you don't even know how the output surface will look like.
zh: 所以你甚至不知道输出表面会是什么样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you don't know how the user might behave with your product, and you also don't know how the LLM might respond to that.
zh: 所以你不知道用户可能如何与你的产品互动，你也不知道 LLM 可能会如何回应。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're now working with an input, output, and a process.
zh: 所以你现在正在处理输入、输出和一个过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't understand all the three very well.
zh: 你不能很好地理解这三者。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're trying to anticipate behavior and build for it.
zh: 你试图预测行为并为此进行构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with agentic systems, this kind of gets even harder.
zh: 对于智能体系统，这变得更加困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's where we talk about the second difference, which is the agency control trade-off.
zh: 这就是我们要讨论的第二个区别，即主观能动性与控制的权衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we mean by that, and I'm kind of shocked so many people don't talk about this.
zh: 我们的意思是，我很震惊那么多人不讨论这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're extremely obsessed with building autonomous systems, agents that can do work for you.
zh: 他们极其痴迷于构建自主系统，可以为你的工作的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: But every time you hand over decision-making capabilities or autonomy to agentic systems, you're kind of relinquishing some amount of control on your end.
zh: 但每次你将决策能力或自主权移交给智能体系统时，你都在某种程度上放弃了一些你的控制权。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you do that, you want to make sure that your agent has gained your trust or it is reliable enough that you can allow it to make decisions.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 领域专家是构建有效的 AI 产品如此重要的一部分，因为你真的需要咨询他们以了解你的 AI 如何表现或理想的行为应该是什么。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: So that kind of an empowering culture always helps.
zh: 所以那种赋能的文化总是有帮助的。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 你想让你的整个组织都参与其中，让 AI 为你工作，而不是试图保卫他们自己的工作等等。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's pull up a visual to show people what the heck we're talking about, and then just walk us through what this is, how this works, how teams can shift the way they build their AI products to this approach to help them avoid a lot of pain and suffering.
zh: 让我们调出一个视觉图来向人们展示我们在讨论什么，然后给我们讲讲这是什么，它是如何工作的，团队如何将他们构建 AI 产品的方式转变为这种方法，以帮助他们避免很多痛苦和折磨。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before we go about explaining the life cycle, a quick story on why Kiriti and I came up with this is because there are tons of companies that we keep talking to that have the pressure from their competitors because they're all building agents.
zh: 在我们解释生命周期之前，讲一个关于为什么 Kiriti 和我提出这个想法的简短故事，因为我们不断与许多公司交谈，它们来自竞争对手的压力，因为它们都在构建智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: We should be building agents that are entirely autonomous.
zh: 我们应该构建完全自主的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I did end up working with a few customers where we built these end-to-end agents.
zh: 我最终确实与一些客户合作，我们构建了这些端到端的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And turns out that because you start off at a place where you don't know how the user might interact with your system and what kind of responses or actions the AI might come up with, it's really hard to fix problems when you have this really huge workflow, which is taking four or five steps, making tons of decisions.
zh: 结果发现，因为你开始的地方不知道用户可能如何与你的系统交互，以及 AI 可能想出什么样的响应或行动，当你有一个真的非常大的工作流，它需要四五步，做出大量决策时，修复问题真的很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just end up debugging so much and then kind of hot fixing to the point where at a time we were building for a customer support use case, which is the example that we give in the newsletter as well.
zh: 你最终会进行大量的调试，然后进行某种热修复，以至于有一次我们为客户支持用例构建，这也是我们在时事通讯中给出的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we had to shut down the product because we were doing so many hot fixes and there was no way we could count all the emerging problems that were coming up.
zh: 而我们不得不关闭该产品，因为我们做了太多的热修复，而且我们无法计算所有出现的新兴问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's also quite some news online.
zh: 而且网上也有相当多的新闻。

speaker: Unknown
en: Recently, I think Air Canada had this thing where one of their agents predicted or hallucinated a policy for a refund, which was not part of their original playbook, and they had to go by it because legal stuff.
zh: 最近，我认为加拿大航空有这样一个事情，他们的一个智能体预测或幻想出了一个退款政策，这不在他们原来的剧本中，他们必须遵守它，因为法律原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there have been a ton of really scary incidents.
zh: 而且已经有非常多真正可怕的 incidents。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's where the idea comes from.
zh: 这就是想法的来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: How can you build so that you don't lose customer trust and you don't end up, or your agent or AI system doesn't end up making decisions that are super dangerous to the company itself.
zh: 你如何构建才能不失去客户的信任，你不会最终，或者你的智能体或 AI 系统不会最终做出对公司本身超级危险的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the same time, build a flywheel so that you can improve your product as you go.
zh: 同时，建立一个飞轮，以便你在进行过程中改进你的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's where we came up with this idea of continuous calibration, continuous development.
zh: 这就是我们提出持续校准、持续开发这个想法的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: The idea is pretty simple, which is we have this right side of the loop, which is continuous development, where you scope capability and curate data, essentially get a data set of what your expected inputs are and what your expected outputs should be looking at.
zh: 这个想法非常简单，即我们在这个循环的右侧，这是持续开发，你在那里界定能力并策展数据，基本上获得一个关于你的预期输入是什么以及你的预期输出应该是什么样的数据集。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a very good exercise before you start building any AI product because many times you figure out that a lot of the folks within the team are just not aligned on how the product should behave.
zh: 在开始构建任何 AI 产品之前，这是一个非常好的练习，因为很多时候你会发现团队中的很多人只是没有就产品应该如何表现达成一致。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's where your PMs can really give in a lot more information and your subject matter experts as well.
zh: 这就是你的产品经理真的可以提供更多信息的地方，以及你的主题专家也是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have this data set that you know your AI product should be doing really well on.
zh: 所以你有这个数据集，你知道你的 AI 产品应该做得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not comprehensive, but it lets you get started.
zh: 它不是全面的，但它让你可以开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you set up the application and then design the right kind of evaluation metrics.
zh: 然后你设置应用程序，然后设计正确的评估指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I intentionally use the term evaluation metrics, although we say evals because I just want to be very specific in what it is because evaluation is a process, evaluation metrics are dimensions that you want to focus on during the process.
zh: 我故意使用评估指标这个术语，虽然我们说评估，因为我只是想非常具体地说明它是什么，因为评估是一个过程，评估指标是你想要在过程中关注的维度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you go about deploying, run your evaluation metrics.
zh: 然后你去部署，运行你的评估指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the second part is the continuous calibration, which is the part where you understand what behavior you hadn't expected in the beginning, right?
zh: 第二部分是持续校准，这是你理解你在一开始没有预料到的行为的部分，对吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because when you start the development process, you have this data set that you're optimizing for, but more often than not, you realize that that data set is not comprehensive enough because users start behaving with your systems in ways that you did not predict.
zh: 因为当你开始开发过程时，你有这个你要优化的数据集，但很多时候，你意识到那个数据集不够全面，因为用户开始以你没有预测到的方式与你的系统互动。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's where you want to do the calibration piece.
zh: 这就是你要做校准的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've deployed my system.
zh: 我已经部署了我的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now I see that there are patterns that I did not really expect and your evaluation metrics should give you some insight into those patterns, but sometimes you figure out that those metrics were also not enough and you probably have new error patterns that you have not thought about.
zh: 现在我看到有一些我真的没有预料到的模式，你的评估指标应该会给你一些关于这些模式的洞察，但有时你会发现那些指标也不够，你可能有一些你没有考虑过的新错误模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's where you analyze your behavior, spot error patterns.
zh: 这就是你分析你的行为，发现错误模式的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: You apply fixes for issues that you see, but you also design newer evaluation metrics to figure out that they are emerging patterns.
zh: 你针对你看到的问题应用修复，但你也设计更新的评估指标以弄清楚它们是新兴模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that doesn't mean you should always design evaluation metrics.
zh: 这并不意味着你应该总是设计评估指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are some errors that you can just fix and not really come back to because they're very spot errors.
zh: 有一些错误你可以直接修复，而不需要真的回头管它们，因为它们是非常具体的错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: For instance, there's a tool calling error just because your tool wasn't defined well and stuff like that.
zh: 例如，有一个工具调用错误，仅仅因为你的工具没有定义好之类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can just fix it and move on.
zh: 你可以直接修复并继续前进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is pretty much how an AI product lifecycle would look like.
zh: 这基本上就是一个 AI 产品生命周期的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what we specifically also mention is while you're going through these iterations, try to think of lower agency iterations in the beginning and higher control iterations.
zh: 但我们特别提到的还有，当你进行这些迭代时，试着在开始时考虑较低主观能动性的迭代，以及较高控制的迭代。

speaker: Unknown
en: What that means is constrain the number of decisions your AI systems can make and make sure that they're humans in the loop and then increase that over time because you're kind of building a flywheel of behavior and you're understanding what kind of use cases are coming in or how your users are using the system.
zh: 这意味着要限制你的 AI 系统可以做出的决策数量，并确保其中有人类参与（人在回路），然后随着时间的推移增加这一点，因为你正在构建一个行为的飞轮，并且你在理解什么样的用例正在进来，或者你的用户如何使用该系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one example I think we give in the newsletter itself is the customer support.
zh: 我认为我们在时事通讯本身中给出的一个例子是客户支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a nice image that kind of shows how you can think of agency and control as two dimensions.
zh: 这是一个很好的图表，展示了如何将主观能动性和控制视为两个维度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And each of your versions keep on increasing the agency or the ability of your AI system to make decisions and lower the control as you go.
zh: 你的每个版本都在不断增加 AI 系统的主观能动性或做出决策的能力，并随着进程降低控制。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one example that we give is that of the customer support agent, where you can break it down into three versions.
zh: 我们给出的一个例子是客户支持智能体，你可以将其分解为三个版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first version is just routing, which is your agent able to classify and route a particular ticket to the right department?
zh: 第一个版本只是路由，即你的智能体能够将特定的工单分类并路由到正确的部门吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes when you read this, you probably think, is it so hard to just do routing?
zh: 有时当你读到这个时，你可能会想，仅仅做路由真的很难吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why can't an agent easily do that?
zh: 为什么智能体不能轻易做到这一点？

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you go to enterprises, routing itself can be a super complex problem.
zh: 当你来到企业时，路由本身可能是一个非常复杂的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Any retail company, any popular retail company that you can think of has hierarchical taxonomies.
zh: 任何零售公司，你能想到的任何流行的零售公司，都有分层级的分类法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most of the times the taxonomies are incredibly messy.
zh: 大多数时候，这些分类法极其混乱。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have worked in use cases where you probably have taxonomy that says some kind of hierarchy and then that says shoes and then women's shoes and men's shoes all at the same layer where idea you should be having shoes and then women's shoes and men's shoes should be subclasses.
zh: 我曾处理过一些用例，你可能有一个分类法，它说的是某种层级结构，然后说鞋子，然后是女鞋和男鞋都在同一层，而本来的想法是你应该有鞋子，然后女鞋和男鞋应该是子类。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you're like, okay, fine.
zh: 然后你会说，好吧，行吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could just merge that.
zh: 我可以把它合并。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you go further and you see that there's also another section on the shoes that says for women and for men, and it's just not aggregated.
zh: 然后你继续往下看，你会发现鞋子下面还有另一个部分，写着给女士和给男士，但这并没有被聚合在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not fixed for some reason.
zh: 由于某种原因，它没有被修复。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if an agent kind of sees this kind of a taxonomy, what is it supposed to do?
zh: 所以如果一个智能体看到了这样的分类法，它应该怎么做？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where is it supposed to route?
zh: 它应该路由到哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of the times we are not aware of these problems until you actually go about building something and understanding it.
zh: 很多时候，我们在实际去构建并理解它之前，并没有意识到这些问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when these kind of problems, real human agents see these kind of problems, they know what to check next.
zh: 当真正的人类智能体看到这类问题时，他们知道接下来要检查什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe they realize that the node that says for women and for men that's under shoes was last updated in 2019, which means that it's just a dead node that's lying there and not being used.
zh: 也许他们意识到，鞋子下面那个写着给女士和给男士的节点上次更新是在 2019 年，这意味着它只是一个躺在那里没有被使用的死节点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they kind of know that, okay, we're supposed to be looking at a different node and stuff like that.
zh: 所以他们大概知道，好的，我们应该查看一个不同的节点之类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm not saying agents cannot understand this or models are not capable enough to understand this, but there are really weird rules within enterprises that are not documented anywhere.
zh: 我并不是说智能体无法理解这一点，或者模型没有足够的能力来理解这一点，但是企业内部确实有一些非常奇怪的规则，任何地方都没有文档记录。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you want to make sure that the agents have all of that context instead of just throwing the problem at that.
zh: 你想确保智能体拥有所有这些上下文，而不是仅仅把问题扔给它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Coming back to the versions we had, routing was one where you have really high control because even if your agent routes to the wrong department, humans can take control and undo those actions.
zh: 回到我们之前说的版本，路由是一个你有非常高控制的版本，因为即使你的智能体路由到了错误的部门，人类也可以接管并撤销这些操作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And along the way, you also figure out that you probably are dealing with a ton of data issues that you need to fix and make sure that your data layer is good enough for the agent to function.
zh: 在此过程中，你还会发现你可能正在处理大量的数据问题，你需要修复这些问题，并确保你的数据层足够好，以便让智能体运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do is what we said of a Copilot, which is now that you've figured out routing works fine after a few iterations and you've fixed all of your data issues, you could go to the next step, which is, can my agent provide suggestions based on some standard operating procedures that we have for the customer support agent?
zh: 我们所做的是就像我们说的副驾驶（Copilot），既然你经过几次迭代后发现路由工作正常，并且你修复了所有的数据问题，你可以进行下一步，即我的智能体能否根据我们为客户支持智能体制定的标准操作程序提供建议？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it could just generate a draft that the human can make changes to.
zh: 它可以生成一个人类可以修改的草稿。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you do this, you're also logging human behavior, which means that how much of this draft was used by the customer support agent or what was omitted.
zh: 当你这样做时，你也在记录人类的行为，这意味着客户支持智能体使用了多少草稿内容，或者省略了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're actually getting error analysis for free when you do this because you're literally logging everything that the user is doing that you could then build back into your flywheel.
zh: 所以当你这样做时，你实际上免费获得了错误分析，因为你确实记录了用户正在做的一切，然后你可以将其构建回你的飞轮中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we say, post that, once you've figured out that those drafts look good and most of the times maybe humans are not making too many changes, they're using these drafts as is.
zh: 然后我们说，在那之后，一旦你发现那些草稿看起来不错，而且大多数时候人类可能没有做太多的修改，他们按原样使用这些草稿。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's when you want to go to your end-to-end resolution assistant that could draft a resolution that could solve the ticket as well.
zh: 那就是你想进入端到端解决助手的时候了，它可以起草一个解决方案，也可以解决该工单。

speaker: Unknown
en: And those are the stages of agency where you start with low agency and then you go up high.
zh: 这些就是主观能动性的阶段，你从低主观能动性开始，然后逐渐升高。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also have this really nice table that we put together, which is what do you do at each version and what you learn that can enable you to go to the next step and what information do you get that you can feed into the loop, right?
zh: 我们还有一个非常好的表格，我们在里面列出了你在每个版本做什么，以及你学到什么可以让你进入下一步，以及你获得什么信息可以反馈到循环中，对吗？
